writing.prompt: Directions: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to write an essay. Suppose you have two options upon graduation: one is to work in a state-owned business and the other in a joint venture. You are to make a choice between the two. Write an essay to explain the reasons for your choice. You should write at least 120 words but no more than 180 words.
writing.sample: When it comes to choosing a career after graduation, I would rather work in a joint venture than in a state-owned business. Though both offer decent prospects, I am firmly convinced that a joint venture suits me better. The main reason is that a joint venture provides a more competitive environment, where personal ability, rather than seniority, decides how far one can go. What attracts me most is the chance to work with foreign colleagues, learn advanced management skills and improve my English in daily practice. Besides, such companies usually offer higher salaries and reward hard work generously, which matters a lot to a fresh graduate like me. A state-owned business, by contrast, tends to be stable but slow, where a young talent may easily be buried by dull routine. For these reasons, I will not hesitate to choose a joint venture, because it offers exactly the growth and challenge that a young person truly needs.

transcript.en: New York State plans to shut off the thundering waters of Niagara Falls—again. At least, the American side of the falls. This "once in a lifetime" event actually may take place twice in some folks' lives. The New York State parks system wants to turn off the falls on the American side sometime in the next two to three years to replace two 115-year-old stone bridges that allow pedestrians, park vehicles and utilities access to Goat Island.
transcript.zh: 纽约州计划再次关闭尼亚加拉大瀑布的雷鸣水流——至少是瀑布的美国一侧。这一"一生一次"的事件实际上可能在某些人的一生中发生两次。纽约州公园系统希望在未来两到三年内关闭美国一侧的瀑布,以更换两座有115年历史的石桥,这些石桥供行人、公园车辆和公用设施通往山羊岛。

transcript.en: The American side of the falls was shut off in 1969 to study the buildup of rock at the base of the falls. When that happened, people came from all over the world to see the falls turned off.
transcript.zh: 美国一侧的瀑布曾在1969年关闭,以研究瀑布底部岩石的堆积情况。当时,世界各地的人们都前来观看瀑布关闭的景象。

transcript.en: People are curious by nature. They want to see what's underneath. In fact, those who first came to have a look did see something. They found millions of coins on the bottom.
transcript.zh: 人们天生充满好奇心。他们想看看下面有什么。事实上,那些最先来观看的人确实看到了一些东西。他们在底部发现了数百万枚硬币。

transcript.en: The Tunisian government said Monday that 45 people have been killed after gunmen attacked a town near the border with Libya.
transcript.zh: 突尼斯政府周一表示,武装分子袭击了与利比亚接壤的一个城镇,造成45人死亡。

transcript.en: The Interior and Defense ministries said that the Tunisian government has closed its two border crossings with Libya because of the attack.
transcript.zh: 内政部和国防部表示,由于这次袭击,突尼斯政府已关闭了与利比亚的两个边境口岸。

transcript.en: The Tunisian military has sent reinforcements and helicopters to the area, and authorities have been hunting several attackers who were still at large.
transcript.zh: 突尼斯军方已向该地区派遣增援部队和直升机,当局一直在追捕几名仍在逃的袭击者。

transcript.en: The violence came amid increasing international concern about Islamic State extremists in Libya. Officials of the Tunisian government are especially worried after dozens of tourists were killed in the attacks in Tunisia last year.
transcript.zh: 这次暴力事件发生之际,国际社会对利比亚的伊斯兰国极端分子的关注日益增加。突尼斯政府官员尤其担忧,因为去年突尼斯发生的袭击事件中有数十名游客丧生。

transcript.en: Defense Minister Farhat Horchani said last week that German and American security experts were expected to come to help Tunisia devise a new electronic video supervision system on its border with Libya.
transcript.zh: 国防部长Farhat Horchani上周表示,预计德国和美国安全专家将前来帮助突尼斯在其与利比亚的边境设计一套新的电子视频监控系统。

transcript.en: Tunisia was targeted last year by three attacks that left 70 people dead and were claimed by Islamic State.
transcript.zh: 突尼斯去年成为三次袭击的目标,造成70人死亡,伊斯兰国宣称对这些袭击负责。

transcript.en: Three university students in Santiago, Chile, have developed a plant-powered device to charge their mobile phones.
transcript.zh: 智利圣地亚哥的三名大学生开发了一种植物供能设备来为他们的手机充电。

transcript.en: The three engineering students got the idea for the device while sitting in their school's courtyard. Their invention is a small biological circuit they call E-Kaia. It captures the energy which plants produce during photosynthesis—a process of converting sunlight into energy.
transcript.zh: 这三名工程专业学生在学校庭院坐着时产生了这个设备的想法。他们的发明是一个被称为E-Kaia的小型生物电路。它捕获植物在光合作用过程中产生的能量——光合作用是一个将阳光转化为能量的过程。

transcript.en: A plant uses only a small part of the energy produced by that process. The rest goes into the soil. E-Kaia collects that energy. The device plugs into the ground and then into a mobile phone.
transcript.zh: 植物只使用该过程产生的一小部分能量。其余的能量进入土壤。E-Kaia收集这些能量。该设备插入地面,然后连接到手机。

transcript.en: The E-Kaia solves two problems for the engineering students. They needed an idea for a class project. They also needed an outlet to plug in their phones.
transcript.zh: E-Kaia为这些工程专业学生解决了两个问题。他们需要一个课程项目的创意。他们也需要一个插座来给手机充电。

transcript.en: One of the student inventors, Camila Rupcich, says the device changes the energy released from the plant into low-level power to charge phones.
transcript.zh: 学生发明者之一Camila Rupcich说,该设备将植物释放的能量转化为低电平电力来给手机充电。

transcript.en: The E-Kaia is able to fully recharge a mobile phone in less than two hours.
transcript.zh: E-Kaia能够在不到两小时内完全充满一部手机。

transcript.en: M: Good morning. What can I do for you?
transcript.zh: M: 早上好。有什么我能帮您的吗?

transcript.en: W: Good morning. Could I talk to Jeffrey Harding please?
transcript.zh: W: 早上好。我能和 Jeffrey Harding 通话吗?

transcript.en: M: Speaking.
transcript.zh: M: 我就是。

transcript.en: W: Hello, Jeff. It's Helen. I got your message on the answering machine. What's the problem?
transcript.zh: W: 你好,Jeff。我是 Helen。我在答录机上收到你的留言了。出什么问题了?

transcript.en: M: Oh, Helen. Well, it's the Grimsby plant again, I'm afraid. The robots on Line 3 have gone wrong. And the line is at a standstill.
transcript.zh: M: 哦,Helen。唉,恐怕又是 Grimsby 工厂的事。3号生产线上的机器人出故障了。整条线都停工了。

transcript.en: W: Can't you replace them with the stand-ins?
transcript.zh: W: 你不能用备用的替换吗?

transcript.en: M: I'm afraid not. The stand-ins are already in use on Line 6. And the ones from Line 6 are being serviced.
transcript.zh: M: 恐怕不行。备用的已经在6号线使用了。而6号线的那些正在维修。

transcript.en: W: When did this happen, Jeff?
transcript.zh: W: 什么时候发生的,Jeff?

transcript.en: M: Well, they've been making a low continuous sound for a day or two. But they finally went dead at 2:30 this afternoon.
transcript.zh: M: 嗯,它们已经发出低沉的持续声响一两天了。但今天下午2点半彻底停了。

transcript.en: W: I see. What did you do? Have you tried the Hall plant?
transcript.zh: W: 我明白了。你怎么处理的?联系过 Hall 工厂吗?

transcript.en: M: Not yet, Helen. I thought I'd better get your OK first.
transcript.zh: M: 还没有,Helen。我想最好先得到你的批准。

transcript.en: W: OK. Get on the phone to Tom, and try to get their stand-ins over tonight. We have to be back at full capacity tomorrow morning. Is it a major job to repair our robots?
transcript.zh: W: 好的。给 Tom 打电话,争取今晚把他们的备用机器人运过来。我们明天早上必须恢复满负荷生产。修我们的机器人是大工程吗?

transcript.en: M: About a week. That's what the maintenance engineer says.
transcript.zh: M: 大约一周。维修工程师是这么说的。

transcript.en: W: Right. Well, if you can get the ones from Hall, please ask Tom to inform Sheffield that he may need their stand-ins in case of emergency during the next week.
transcript.zh: W: 好。那如果你能从 Hall 拿到备用的,请让 Tom 通知 Sheffield,他下周可能需要他们的备用机器人以备不时之需。

transcript.en: M: OK. Thank you very much, Helen.
transcript.zh: M: 好的。非常感谢你,Helen。

transcript.en: W: You are most welcome.
transcript.zh: W: 不客气。

transcript.en: M: Sorry to spoil your day off.
transcript.zh: M: 抱歉打扰你休息日了。

transcript.en: W: It doesn't matter.
transcript.zh: W: 没关系。

transcript.en: W: This is Kerry Burke from New York Daily News. I'm speaking to Delroy Simmonds, an unemployed Brooklyn man who missed a job interview Tuesday for the best of reasons: He was saving the life of a 9-month-old boy who was blown into the path of an oncoming subway train by a high wind.
transcript.zh: W: 我是《纽约每日新闻》的Kerry Burke。我正在采访Delroy Simmonds，一位布鲁克林的失业男子，他周二错过了一场工作面试，原因再好不过了：他救了一名9个月大的男婴，这个孩子被大风吹到了即将进站的地铁轨道上。

transcript.en: M: Everybody is making me out to be some sort of superhero. I'm just an ordinary person, and a father of two. Anybody in that situation would have done what I did.
transcript.zh: M: 大家都把我当成什么超级英雄似的。我只是个普通人，两个孩子的父亲。任何人在那种情况下都会做我做的事。

transcript.en: W: You were going to an interview when the incident occurred, right?
transcript.zh: W: 事发时你正要去面试，对吗？

transcript.en: M: Yes, I was on my way to apply for a maintenance position. I've been looking for a job for a year and more. I'm looking for something to support my family.
transcript.zh: M: 对，我当时正去应聘一个维修工的职位。我找工作已经一年多了。我想找份工作养家。

transcript.en: W: Tell us what happened at the station.
transcript.zh: W: 跟我们说说车站发生了什么。

transcript.en: M: There was a strong wind. It had to be 30 to 40 miles an hour. There was a woman with four kids. One was in a pushchair. The wind blew the baby onto the tracks.
transcript.zh: M: 当时风很大。肯定有每小时三四十英里。有个女人带着四个孩子。一个在婴儿车里。风把婴儿吹到了轨道上。

transcript.en: W: Witnesses said people were looking on in horror as the child's mother, identified by sources as Maria Zamara, stood frozen in shock. In the distance, people could see the train rounding a bend, headed into the station. I guess you were not aware of any of these, right?
transcript.zh: W: 目击者说人们惊恐地看着，孩子的母亲，据消息来源确认是Maria Zamara，吓得呆住了。远处能看到火车转过弯道，朝车站驶来。我猜你当时没注意到这些，对吧？

transcript.en: M: No. I just jumped down and grabbed the baby. The train was coming around the corner as I lifted the baby from the tracks. I really wasn't thinking.
transcript.zh: M: 没有。我就跳下去抱起了婴儿。我把婴儿从轨道上抱起来的时候火车正转过弯来。我当时真没多想。

transcript.en: W: What an amazing story! Thank you very much.
transcript.zh: W: 真是个了不起的故事！非常感谢。

transcript.en: There's one sound that gets a big reaction from kids on a hot day, the sound of an ice-cream truck.
transcript.zh: 在炎热的日子里，有一种声音能引起孩子们的强烈反应，那就是冰淇淋车的声音。

transcript.en: Maria McCartney has been in the mobile ice-cream business since 2005.
transcript.zh: Maria McCartney 自2005年以来一直从事流动冰淇淋生意。

transcript.en: "When I was a little girl, I saw an ice-cream truck and knew I wanted to have one someday," McCartney said.
transcript.zh: McCartney 说："当我还是个小女孩的时候，我看到了一辆冰淇淋车，就知道我有朝一日想拥有一辆。"

transcript.en: During the hot days of summer, Maria and her daughter drive an ice-cream truck through neighborhoods and parks in Billings.
transcript.zh: 在夏日炎炎的日子里，Maria 和她的女儿开着冰淇淋车穿梭于 Billings 的街区和公园。

transcript.en: It's not about making money for this former elementary school teacher. Rather, she wants to preserve the tradition of the neighborhood ice-cream truck.
transcript.zh: 对于这位前小学教师来说，这不是为了赚钱，而是她想保留街区冰淇淋车这一传统。

transcript.en: "Truly my favorite part is to see the kids jumping up and down and they just get so excited. It's great to build a memory for them too. There are not a lot of these ice-cream trucks around anymore. The parents come out barefoot and screaming, ready to buy ice-cream; they remember when they were kids and they saw a truck," she said.
transcript.zh: 她说："我最喜欢的部分真的是看到孩子们上蹿下跳，他们是那么兴奋。为他们建立一段回忆也很棒。现在已经没有多少这样的冰淇淋车了。家长们光着脚跑出来，尖叫着，准备买冰淇淋；他们记得自己小时候看到冰淇淋车的情景。"

transcript.en: While the treats may be ice-cold, Maria has a warm heart for little faces. Her truck features a donation bucket for kids who don't have money for ice-cream.
transcript.zh: 虽然这些冷饮冰凉刺骨，但 Maria 对小脸蛋们却有一颗温暖的心。她的车上设有一个捐款桶，专为没钱买冰淇淋的孩子准备。

transcript.en: "When there are three kids and only two of them have money, I always make sure the third one gets something because I can't drive away and have that third one not have something," she said.
transcript.zh: 她说："当有三个孩子，但只有两个人有钱时，我总是确保第三个孩子也能得到点什么，因为我不能就这样开走，让第三个孩子什么都没有。"

transcript.en: We know we have to pay for what we get. If we buy food, we have to pay for it. If a doctor treats us, we know there will be a bill to pay. These are private bills. But there are also public bills to be paid. They are paid by the government. In turn we get the needed services. We pay for these services through taxes.
transcript.zh: 我们知道必须为所得之物付费。如果我们购买食物,就必须为此付款。如果医生为我们治病,我们知道会有账单要付。这些是私人账单。但也有公共账单需要支付。它们由政府支付。反过来我们获得所需的服务。我们通过税收为这些服务付费。

transcript.en: What would happen if everyone stopped paying taxes? The water supply would stop; the streets might not be cleaned; schools would be closed. We would not want to live in such a city. The chief duty of every government is to protect persons and property. More than three-fourths of government expenses are used for this purpose. The next largest amount of public money goes to teach and train our citizens. Billions of dollars each year are spent on schools and libraries. Also, a large amount of public funds is spent on roads.
transcript.zh: 如果每个人都停止纳税会发生什么?供水会停止;街道可能不会被清扫;学校会关闭。我们不会想生活在这样的城市里。每个政府的首要职责是保护人身和财产。超过四分之三的政府支出用于此目的。公共资金的第二大用途是教育和培训我们的公民。每年数十亿美元花费在学校和图书馆上。此外,大量公共资金用于道路建设。

transcript.en: Most of the needed funds are raised by taxes. The law orders us to pay taxes. We have no choice in the matter.
transcript.zh: 所需资金的大部分通过税收筹集。法律要求我们纳税。在这件事上我们别无选择。

transcript.en: Years ago the government made money by selling public lands. But most of the best public lands have now been sold. There are still some public lands that contain oil, coal and other natural resources. They could be sold, but we want to save them for future years. So we all must pay our share for the services that make our lives comfortable.
transcript.zh: 多年前政府通过出售公共土地来赚钱。但现在大部分最好的公共土地已经出售。仍有一些含有石油、煤炭和其他自然资源的公共土地。它们可以出售,但我们想为未来保留它们。因此我们都必须为使我们生活舒适的服务支付我们应尽的份额。

transcript.en: Did you know that, besides larger places like France and Germany, Europe is home to several extremely tiny countries? One of these countries contains less than a square mile of land. Another is surrounded on all sides by Italy. Yet each is an independent land, with its own government, trade, and customs.
transcript.zh: 你知道吗,除了法国和德国这样的较大国家之外,欧洲还有几个极小的国家。其中一个国家的面积不到一平方英里,另一个则四面被意大利包围。然而每个国家都是独立的领土,拥有自己的政府、贸易和海关。

transcript.en: One of the best known of these small countries is Monaco. It is situated on the Mediterranean Sea and surrounded by France on three sides. Monaco became familiar to Americans when its ruler, Prince Rainier, married the American actress Grace Kelly. Rainier's family has ruled Monaco almost continuously since 1297. The land has been independent for over three hundred years.
transcript.zh: 这些小国中最著名的是摩纳哥。它位于地中海沿岸,三面被法国环绕。当摩纳哥的统治者雷尼尔亲王与美国女演员Grace Kelly结婚时,美国人开始熟悉这个国家。雷尼尔的家族自1297年以来几乎一直统治着摩纳哥。这片土地已经独立三百多年了。

transcript.en: Andorra, with an area of some 200 square miles, is considerably larger than Monaco. This country is located in the Pyrenees Mountains, with France on one side and Spain on the other. Potatoes and tobacco are grown in Andorra's steep mountain valleys. One of the products it exports is clothing. Andorra is also known for its excellent skiing locations.
transcript.zh: 安道尔面积约200平方英里,比摩纳哥大得多。这个国家位于比利牛斯山脉,一边是法国,另一边是西班牙。安道尔陡峭的山谷中种植着土豆和烟草。它出口的产品之一是服装。安道尔还以其优越的滑雪场地而闻名。

transcript.en: Within the Alps in Central Europe is Liechtenstein, a tiny country of about 30,000 people who speak mostly German. Liechtenstein uses the same money as its neighbor Switzerland, but it has been an independent country since the 1860s. Taxes are low, so many businesses have their headquarters here. The country makes and exports a lot of machinery. Other small, independent states in Europe are San Marino and Luxembourg. Each of these has unique qualities as well.
transcript.zh: 位于中欧阿尔卑斯山脉内的列支敦士登是一个约有三万人口的小国,人们主要讲德语。列支敦士登使用与邻国瑞士相同的货币,但自19世纪60年代以来一直是一个独立国家。由于税收较低,许多企业将总部设在这里。该国制造并出口大量机械。欧洲其他独立小国还有圣马力诺和卢森堡。这些国家各有独特之处。

matching.title: The Secret to Raising Smart Kids

paragraphs.t: I first began to investigate the basis of human motivation—and how people persevere after setbacks—as a psychology graduate student at Yale University in the 1960s. Animal experiments by psychologists at the University of Pennsylvania had shown that after repeated failures, most animals conclude that a situation is hopeless and beyond their control. After such an experience an animal often remains passive even when it can effect change—a state they called learned helplessness.

People can learn to be helpless, too. Why do some students give up when they encounter difficulty, whereas others who are no more skilled continue to strive and learn? One answer, I soon discovered, lay in people's beliefs about why they had failed.

In particular, attributing poor performance to a lack of ability depresses motivation more than does the belief that lack of effort is to blame. When I told a group of school children who displayed helpless behavior that a lack of effort led to their mistakes in math, they learned to keep trying when the problems got tough. Another group of helpless children who were simply rewarded for their success on easier problems did not improve their ability to solve hard math problems. These experiments indicated that a focus on effort can help resolve helplessness and generate success.

Later, I developed a broader theory of what separates the two general classes of learners—helpless versus mastery-oriented. I realized these different types of students not only explain their failures differently, but they also hold different "theories" of intelligence. The helpless ones believe intelligence is a fixed characteristic: you have only a certain amount, and that's that. I call this a "fixed mind-set(思维模式)." Mistakes crack their self-confidence because they attribute errors to a lack of ability, which they feel powerless to change. They avoid challenges because challenges make mistakes more likely. The mastery- oriented children, on the other hand, think intelligence is not fixed and can be developed through education and hard work. Such children believe challenges are energizing rather than intimidating(令人生畏); they offer opportunities to learn. Students with such a growth mind-set were destined( 注定) for greater academic success and were quite likely to outperform their counterparts.

We validated these expectations in a study in which two other psychologists and I monitored 373 students for two years during the transition to junior high school, when the work gets more difficult and the grading more strict, to determine how their mind-sets might affect their math grades. At the beginning of seventh grade, we assessed the students' mind-sets by asking them to agree or disagree with statements such as "Your intelligence is something very basic about you that you can't really change." We then assessed their beliefs about other aspects of learning and looked to see what happened to their grades.

As predicted, the students with a growth mind-set felt that learning was a more important goal than getting good grades. In addition, they held hard work in high regard. They understood that even geniuses have to work hard. Confronted by a setback such as a disappointing test grade, students with a growth mind-set said they would study harder or try a different strategy. The students who held a fixed mind-set, however, were concerned about looking smart with less regard for learning. They had negative views of effort, believing that having to work hard was a sign of low ability. They thought that a person with talent or intelligence did not need to work hard to do well. Attributing a bad grade to their own lack of ability, those with a fixed mind- set said that they would study less in the future, try never to take that subject again and consider cheating on future tests.

Such different outlooks had a dramatic impact on performance. At the start of junior high, the math achievement test scores of the students with a growth mind-set were comparable to those of students who displayed a fixed mind-set. But as the work became more difficult, the students with a growth mind-set showed greater persistence. As a result, their math grades overtook those of the other students by the end of the first semester—and the gap between the two groups continued to widen during the two years we followed them.

A fixed mind-set can also hinder communication and progress in the workplace and discourage or ignore constructive criticism and advice. Research shows that managers who have a fixed mind-set are less likely to seek or welcome feedback from their employees than are managers with a growth mind-set.

How do we transmit a growth mind-set to our children? One way is by telling stories about achievements that result from hard work. For instance, talking about mathematical geniuses who were more or less born that way puts students in a fixed mind-set, but descriptions of great mathematicians who fell in love with math and developed amazing skills produce a growth mind-set.

In addition, parents and teachers can help children by providing explicit instruction regarding the mind as a learning machine. I designed an eight-session workshop for 91 students whose math grades were declining in their first year of junior high. Forty-eight of the students received instruction in study skills only, whereas the others attended a combination of study skills sessions and classes in which they learned about the growth mind-set and how to apply it to schoolwork. In the growth mind-set classes, students read and discussed an article entitled "You Can Grow Your Brain." They were taught that the brain is like a muscle that gets stronger with use and that learning prompts the brain to grow new connections. From such instruction, many students began to see themselves as agents of their own brain development. Despite being unaware that there were two types of instruction, teachers reported significant motivational changes in 27% of the children in the growth mind-set workshop as compared with only 9% of students in the control group.
Research is converging(汇聚) on the conclusion that great accomplishment and even genius are typically the result of years of passion and dedication and not something that flows naturally from a gift.

questions.s: The author's experiment shows that students with a fixed mind-set believe having to work hard is an indication of low ability.
Focusing on effort is effective in helping children overcome frustration and achieve success.
We can cultivate a growth mind-set in children by telling success stories that emphasize hard work and love of learning.
Students' belief about the cause of their failure explains their attitude toward setbacks.
In the author's experiment, students with a growth mind-set showed greater perseverance in solving difficult math problems.
The author conducted an experiment to find out about the influence of students' mind-sets on math learning.
After failing again and again, most animals give up hope.
Informing students about the brain as a learning machine is a good strategy to enhance their motivation for learning.
People with a fixed mind-set believe that one's intelligence is unchangeable.
In the workplace, feedback may not be so welcome to managers with a fixed mind-set.

careful.passage: "Sugar, alcohol and tobacco," economist Adam Smith once wrote, "are commodities which are nowhere necessaries of life, which have become objects of almost universal consumption, and which are, therefore, extremely popular subjects of taxation." Two and a half centuries on, most countries impose some sort of tax on alcohol and tobacco. With surging obesity levels putting increasing strain on public health systems, governments around the world have begun to toy with the idea of taxing sugar as well. Whether such taxes work is a matter of debate. A preliminary review of Mexico's taxation found a fall in purchases of taxed drinks as well as a rise in sales of untaxed and healthier drinks. By contrast, a Danish tax on foods high in fats was abandoned a year after its introduction, amid claims that consumers were avoiding it by crossing the border to Germany to satisfy their desire for cheaper, fattier fare. The food industry has, in general, been firmly opposed to such direct government action. Nonetheless, the renewed focus on waistlines means that industry groups are under pressure to demonstrate their products are healthy as well as tasty. Over the past three decades, the industry has made some efforts to improve the quality of its offerings. For example, some drink manufacturers have cut the amount of sugar in their beverages. Many of the reductions over the past 30 years have been achieved either by reducing the amount of sugar, salt or fat in a product, or by finding an alternative ingredient. More recently, however, some companies have been investing money in a more ambitious undertaking: learning how to adjust the fundamental make-up of the food they sell. For example, having salt on the outside, but none on the inside, reduces the salt content without changing the taste. While reformulating recipes(配方) is one way to improve public health, it should be part of a multi-sided approach. The key is to remember that there is not just one solution. To deal with obesity, a mixture of approaches—including reformulation, taxation and adjusting portion sizes—will be needed. There is no silver bullet.

questions.s: What did Adam Smith say about sugar, alcohol and tobacco?

o.t: They were profitable to manufacture.
They were in ever-increasing demand.
They were subject to taxation almost everywhere.
They were no longer considered necessities of life.

questions.s: Why have many countries started to consider taxing sugar?

o.t: They are under growing pressure to balance their national budgets.
They find it ever harder to cope with sugar-induced health problems.
The practice of taxing alcohol and tobacco has proved both popular and profitable.
The sugar industry is overtaking alcohol and tobacco business in generating profits.

questions.s: What do we learn about Danish taxation on fat-rich foods?

o.t: It did not work out as well as was expected.
It gave rise to a lot of problems on the border.
It could not succeed without German cooperation.
It met with firm opposition from the food industry.

questions.s: What is the more recent effort by food companies to make foods and drinks both healthy and tasty?

o.t: Replacing sugar or salt with alternative ingredients.
Setting a limit on the amount of sugar or salt in their products.
Investing in research to find ways to adapt to consumers' needs.
Adjusting the physical composition of their products.

 7)?

o.t: There is no single easy quick solution to the problem.
There is no hope of success without public cooperation.
There is no hurry in finding ways to solve the obesity problem.

careful.passage: You may have heard some of the fashion industry horror stories: models eating tissues or cotton balls to hold off hunger, and models collapsing from hunger-induced heart attacks just seconds after they step off the runway. Excessively skinny models have been a point of controversy for decades, and two researchers say a model's body mass should be a workplace health and safety issue. In an editorial released Monday in the American Journal of Public Health, Katherine Record and Bryn Austin made their case for government regulation of the fashion industry. The average international runway model has a body mass index (BMI) under 16—low enough to indicate starvation by the World Health Organization's standard. And Record and Austin are worried not just about the models themselves, but about the vast number of girls and women their images influence. "Especially girls and teens," says Record. "Seventy percent of girls aged 10 to 18 report that they define perfect body image based on what they see in magazines." That's especially worrying, she says, given that anorexia(厌食症) results in more deaths than does any other mental illness, according to the National Institute of Mental Health. It's commonly known that certain diseases are linked with occupations like lung disease in coal miners. Professional fashion models are particularly vulnerable to eating disorders resulting from occupational demands to maintain extreme thinness. Record's suggestion is to prohibit agents from hiring models with a BMI below 18. In April, France passed a law setting lower limits for a model's weight. Agents and fashion houses who hire models with a BMI under 18 could pay $82,000 in fines and spend up to 6 months in jail. Regulating the fashion industry in the United States won't be easy, Record says. But with the new rules in France, U.S. support could make a difference. "A designer can't survive without participating in Paris Fashion Week", she says, adding, "Our argument is that the same would be true of New York Fashion Week."

questions.s: What do Record and Austin say about fashion models' body mass?

o.t: It has caused needless controversy.
It is but a matter of personal taste.
It is the focus of the modeling business.
It affects models' health and safety.

questions.s: What are Record and Austin advocating in the Monday editorial?

o.t: A change in the public's view of female beauty.
Government legislation about models' weight.
Elimination of forced weight loss by models.
Prohibition of models eating non-food stuff.

questions.s: Why are Record and Austin especially worried about the low body mass index of models?

o.t: It contributes to many mental illnesses.
It defines the future of the fashion industry.
It has great influence on numerous girls and women.
It keeps many otherwise qualified women off the runway.

questions.s: What do we learn about France's fashion industry?

o.t: It has difficulty hiring models.
It now has a new law to follow.
It allows girls under 18 on the runway.
It has overtaken that of the United States.

questions.s: What does Record expect of New York Fashion Week?

o.t: It will create a completely new set of rules.
It will do better than Paris Fashion Week.
It will differ from Paris Fashion Week.
It will have models with a higher BMI.

translation.source: 随着中国的改革开放,如今很多年轻人都喜欢举行西式婚礼。新娘在婚礼上穿着白色婚纱,因为白色被认为 是纯洁的象征。然而,在中国传统文化中,白色经常是葬礼上使用的颜色。因此务必记住,白花一定不要用作祝人 康复的礼物,尤其不要送给老年人或危重病人。同样,礼金也不能装在白色的信封里,而要装在红色的信封里。
translation.reference: With China’s reform and opening-up, many young people today prefer to hold Western-style weddings. The bride wears a white wedding dress at the wedding, because white is regarded as a symbol of purity. However, in traditional Chinese culture, white is often the color used at funerals. Therefore, please bear in mind that white flowers should never be used as a gift to wish someone a quick recovery, and especially should not be given to the elderly or the seriously ill. Similarly, gift money should not be put in a white envelope, but rather in a red one.
